annotations.shape: one text/plain us-ascii message with two Content-Type fields (text/plain; charset=us-ascii then text/html; charset=utf-8); identity is by ordinal (D2) and the first wins
annotations.raw_fixture: hand-written bytes in tools/write_raw_fixtures.py, frozen in fixtures/raw/SHA256SUMS -- a duplicate-header mutation the generator would have to encode
annotations.phase_0_facts: container.*, headers.fields (eight fields: the two Content-Type lines are ordinals 6 and 7), part.tree, part.regions, part.gaps, body.preamble_epilogue, decode.chain (which reads the FIRST Content-Type: text/plain, us-ascii) and body.content_sha256
annotations.phase_1_facts: headers.projection over all eight fields and the gap headers.duplicate_header, which the walker does not emit today and so rides in gaps.later
annotations.labels_are_typed: every value was read out of the fixture bytes with a hex-editor-style line dump and typed by a model from the RFC and design rules (D2/D9), never copied out of the walker; labels_provenance is spec because a model wrote them, not a person
annotations.span_conventions: a field's raw_span covers its line including the line ending; value_span starts immediately after the colon and keeps the leading space; a part's headers_span includes its closing empty line
annotations.expected_gaps: headers.duplicate_header (Phase 1, in gaps.later) on part 1; no phase-0 gap
annotations.not_yet_labelled: addresses, the Date projection, encoded words, body views, attachments, statuses, thread edges and TimeEvents

value: two Content-Type fields that disagree (text/plain vs text/html); walk._header_value takes the first, so the duplicate is recorded as a gap rather than dropped silently
